title: HARNESS (not a product defect): confirm_and_run waits 900s for a download phase that can no longer occur
detail: flows.confirm_and_run waited on condition download_running, which reads the step tracker for active.id=='download'. A course that delivers in under a second reaches the completion screen before a 2.0s poll can observe step 4, so the wait can never be satisfied and burns its full 900s timeout; the terminal check that follows returns with waited_s 0.0. Measured on m010 (course 43667, one ExternalUrl): engine logged Course Finished at 17:49:47, flow returned 18:04:51 - 958s row time for under a second of work. It is a race, so it hit 1 of the first 9 rows. m011's comparable 981s is genuine zip-extraction work and is NOT this: it has its phase_download capture, and m010 is the only row missing one. FIXED in this run - new condition download_running_or_done stops on running OR terminal, and the phase capture is gated on running so a completion screen is never filed as evidence of the download phase. Validated both directions live: silent on a non-download screen, done at waited_s 0.0 on a terminal screen, and a fresh row still produced its phase_download capture.

title: HARNESS (not a product defect): set_size_cap resolved Save by accessible name instead of the key the app provides
detail: ui/auth.py keys the Settings dialog primary action stg_btn_save with a comment stating it did so 'so the live audit can drive it'. flows.set_size_cap instead did dlg.get_by_role('button', name='Save Settings').count() - a SINGLE sample against an accessibility tree that the preceding number-input Enter commit rebuilds. It killed the first row of two lanes with 'Save Settings button not found in the dialog' against a dialog that renders it correctly (verified by hand on the same build). Now waits on the key via _await_key. Validated: Max file size: 5 MB reaches the engine parameter line, and both previously-failed rows passed on retry.

title: HARNESS (not a product defect): open_custom clicked the primary action without waiting for the CSS selection gate
detail: The download page's primary actions sit OUTSIDE the course-list fragment, so disabled= cannot see a tick made inside it; availability is published by a components.html bridge as data-cd-has-sel on BODY (ui/course_selector._gate_actions_on_selection). That bridge is an iframe whose boot is not synchronous with the tick React has already committed, so set_checkbox can VERIFY a course is selected in the same frame the gate still reads 'nothing selected' - which is exactly what the failure recorded: gated True, found True, disabled False. Measured on the parent app: with nothing ticked the gate stays closed across repeated samples, and it lifts immediately once a course is genuinely ticked, so the wait cannot pass falsely. open_custom now polls pointer-events on the button itself (the property a user's pointer meets) rather than the attribute behind it, and a timeout still raises with the full probe.

title: SCOPE: gpu lane (9 rows) not run - download matrix coverage is 95.1% pairwise, not 100%
detail: Run at the user's instruction (no GPU on this machine; mp4 too costly). Measured consequence: 47 of 56 rows executed, 2-way coverage 777/817 = 95.1%. The 40 lost pairs are NOT confined to Panopto, because matrix.classify sends a row needing BOTH gpu and office to gpu, so those rows also carried Office-conversion combinations: mode=flat x convert_pptx, file_filter=study x convert_word, mode=flat x dl_quizzes, mode=flat x dl_submissions, pan_layout=separate x dl_announcements among them. Worth knowing for next time: on this course set the 9 rows would have done NO GPU or mp4 work at all - O5 reports 0 recordings for 43667/45899/43665 and the plan already lists panopto under unreachable_requirements - so their only real cost was ~94 min of ordinary Canvas file downloading. If those Office pairs matter, the cheap fix is to re-run just the gpu-lane rows, not to re-run the matrix.

title: HARNESS (not a product defect): a bridged INFO progress note was reported as a medium robustness defect
detail: oracles/log.py classifies a line as 'suspicious' on the WORD 'failed' appearing in the payload, without reading the log LEVEL. Panopto discovery on a course with no recordings logs, at INFO, 'GetFolders failed for folder <id>: HTTP 500 ... User unified\<CANVAS_USER> is not in role (FolderEnumerate)' - one probe inside a documented fallback chain. The chain then resolves the folder by another route, logs an unscoped probe reading TotalNumber=3082 (its own comment explains this proves auth works and the problem is folder-scoped), reports 'Discovered 0 recording(s)' - the CORRECT answer, O5 confirms 43667/45899/43665 all have 0 - and closes 'Course Finished | Errors: 0'. The app's own convention (CLAUDE.md, the swallowed-analysis-hook rule) is that a real problem is logged at WARNING or above. FIXED by DOWNGRADING, not dropping: nothing else in the suite reports this channel, so deleting the event would be an under-report if an INFO line ever carried a real failure. oracles/log.py now carries 'raw' on each unexpected entry - the first version of this fix matched on 'msg', which has the level prefix stripped, so it could never have fired. Swept over all 73 logs in the corpus: moves exactly these 3 events out of the defect pile and leaves every other unexpected event, including a genuine high COM Error, reported unchanged.

title: HARNESS (not a product defect): a row was judged against config the driver never applied - fabricated a HIGH
detail: m014 asked for convert_excel=True. flows.configure recorded 'control not present (card collapsed?)' for convert_excel, convert_html, convert_code, convert_urls and convert_video - the app was never told to convert anything. Its contract therefore correctly recorded convert_excel=False and it correctly left all 50 .xlsx alone. Because crosscheck received expect=job.config (what was REQUESTED, not what was applied), that correct behaviour produced three findings: 1 high 'Converter convert_excel was set to True but the folder contract says False', plus 'convert_excel enabled but 50 source file(s) survived conversion' and 'Excel conversion enabled but no _Data.txt sidecar produced'. Same class as RUNBOOK checker-defect 9 (the size cap accepted into every row and applied to none). Frequency measured: 1 of 23 rows. TWO fixes. (1) parallel.expect_for() drops any factor the row's own trace reports as unapplied, and is shared by the live pass AND recheck so they cannot drift - the reason seed_expectations exists on the sync side; the factor is DROPPED, not set False, because _conversions and the OFF-must-not-consume mirror check both skip an absent key while a False would assert the opposite expectation just as wrongly. An observation finding names the skipped factors so a narrowed expectation can never become a silent PASS. (2) set_toggle now polls before believing 'not present' (a rerun in flight makes a re-rendering card look collapsed) and _set_toggle_in_card re-opens the card once if it genuinely closed. Validated both directions on stored evidence: fires on m014, silent on m013.

title: CONFIRMED GOOD: a real Excel COM failure did NOT delete the user's original workbook
detail: Reproduced live, not synthetically. The office lane hit '[ERROR] [converters.excel] [COM] Excel init failed: (-2146959355, Server-udfoerelse mislykkedes)' = CO_E_SERVER_EXEC_FAILURE, followed by '[ERROR] [converters.post_processing] ekstraopgave 1 - VL.xlsx  Conversion timed out after 180s (Excel stopped responding)'. O3 then shows the source STILL PRESENT at 'Ekstra traening (traening i gl. eksamensopgaver)/ekstraopgave 1 - VL.xlsx', with its 'ekstraopgave 1 - VL_Data.txt' sidecar beside it. This is the exact condition the 2026-08-08 hardening was written for ('An Office converter deletes the user's original - so the PDF must be PROVEN first'): the COM call did not raise cleanly, no usable PDF was produced, pdf_looks_real refused the delete and the workbook was kept. The run also continued to later files rather than aborting the phase, which is _run_phase's isolation doing its job. Worth recording as evidence that the guard holds against a REAL Office failure and not only against a seeded stub.

title: FOLLOW-UP (attribution uncertain): a COM-spawned EXCEL.EXE outlived its row by ~1h45m while a later init failed
detail: Measured at 19:05 during the office lane: TWO EXCEL.EXE, both 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\Root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE /automation -Embedding', both with ParentProcessId 1396 (DCOM/RPCSS - CLAUDE.md notes a COM-spawned Office is not our child, which is why the session orphan reaper cannot see one). CreationDate 20260808172055 for the first and 20260808190111 for the second. The office lane converts one workbook at a time, and the first instance predates the current row by about 1h45m, spanning several rows. The 19:01:11 instance appeared 3 seconds after '[COM] Excel init failed: CO_E_SERVER_EXEC_FAILURE', and that row's conversion then timed out after 180s. Consistent with a wedged/orphaned instance holding the machine-wide Excel Application object, which is the class the 2026-08-08 _init_app fix addresses (capture the PID immediately after DispatchEx, guard the property sets, _kill_app on failure). DELIBERATELY NOT FILED AS A PRODUCT DEFECT: this audit was running three lanes on a 13.9 GB machine with 2.6-3.0 GB free, and CO_E_SERVER_EXEC_FAILURE is equally a classic low-resource symptom, so the environment is a live alternative explanation I cannot exclude from this evidence. To settle it, re-run the office lane ALONE with memory headroom and watch whether an EXCEL.EXE survives a completed row; a surviving instance with no lane converting would be conclusive.

title: A COM-spawned EXCEL.EXE outlived 4+ rows (2h08m) while the app correctly killed every instance it tracked
detail: REFINES the earlier 'attribution uncertain' note by separating two phenomena I had conflated. The HANGS are plausibly aggravated by this audit's memory pressure (3 lanes on a 13.9 GB machine). The LEAK is not: memory pressure does not explain a process outliving its owner. Measured directly. The app spawns one Excel per conversion attempt and reclaims a hung one by PID - in row m028 alone it logged 'Excel hung >180s on <file>. Killing PID 26740 / 21420 / 27204', three different PIDs, all gone. Yet EXCEL.EXE PID 20872, CreationDate 20260808172055, was still alive at 19:29 - 2h08m, spanning at least m012, m013, m014 and m028. Its command line is 'EXCEL.EXE /automation -Embedding' with ParentProcessId 1396 (DCOM/RPCSS), so it is COM-launched and headless, NOT a user's own Excel window, and CLAUDE.md notes the session orphan reaper cannot see it precisely because it is a child of DCOM rather than of us. This is the class the 2026-08-08 _init_app hardening addresses (capture the PID immediately after DispatchEx, guard the property sets, _kill_app on failure) - one instance reachable from neither direction. User-visible consequence: a ~175 MB headless Excel that never exits, per occurrence, for the life of the session. NOT tied to a specific row by this evidence - 20872 appeared at 17:20:55, inside m014's window, which is a row whose convert_excel toggle was never applied, so the trigger is worth pinning down before fixing. To reproduce cleanly: run the office lane alone and watch for an EXCEL.EXE that survives a COMPLETED row.

title: TRIAGE: the 10 HIGH Excel COM errors on m028 are ENVIRONMENTAL (audit-induced), not product defects
detail: Every blocking finding in this run comes from ONE row, m028_c43665, and every one is the generic 'unexpected bridged_error' net firing on Excel COM failures: four '[COM Timeout] Excel hung >180s on <workbook>. Killing PID <n>', the matching four 'Conversion timed out after 180s', one '[COM] Excel init failed: CO_E_SERVER_EXEC_FAILURE' and one 'ekstraopgave 1 - VL.xlsx Conversion failed twice'. CONTROLLED COMPARISON settles the cause: m014 re-ran the SAME course (43665) over the SAME 50 workbooks about three hours later, after the two free lanes had exited and free memory went from 2.6-3.0 GB to 5+ GB, and logged ZERO timeouts. The audit was running three lanes on a 13.9 GB machine; CO_E_SERVER_EXEC_FAILURE and headless Excel hangs are classic low-resource symptoms. So the trigger is the harness's own concurrency, not the app. WHAT THE APP DID, and it is the reason these are worth keeping in the record rather than deleting: it detected each hang, force-killed that specific PID (a different pid each time, so no instance was orphaned by this path), retried, RECOVERED 3 of the 4, kept the original of the one that failed twice - the 2026-08-08 pdf_looks_real gate refusing to delete a source without a proven PDF - and reported '1 file could not be converted' on the completion screen with the likely cause and the remedy. O1, O3 and the log all agree at 1. Recommend marking these classes 'invalid' in the register with this note, so a future run does not re-chase them; the separate EXCEL.EXE LEAK finding is NOT covered by this verdict and remains open, because memory pressure does not explain a process outliving its owner.

title: CONFIRMED LEAK: the orphaned EXCEL.EXE survived the entire audit - 5h54m, outliving every lane, the app and the browser
detail: Decisive follow-up to the earlier 'attribution uncertain' note, taken AFTER full teardown. At 23:15, with zero audit Streamlit apps and zero audit Chrome processes remaining, EXCEL.EXE PID 20872 (CreationDate 20260808172055, command line 'EXCEL.EXE /automation -Embedding', ParentProcessId 1396 = DCOM/RPCSS) was STILL RUNNING - 5 hours 54 minutes old. It outlived all 12 office-lane rows, the app that spawned it, and the browser. That excludes the last benign explanation: it cannot be an instance a live conversion was using, because nothing was live. It is also not the user's own Excel - '/automation -Embedding' means COM-launched and headless. Contrast with the instances the app DOES track: during m028 it logged '[COM Timeout] Excel hung >180s ... Killing PID 26740 / 21420 / 27204', three different pids, every one reclaimed. So the app reclaims what it holds a handle or pid for, and 20872 was reachable from neither - exactly the failure the 2026-08-08 _init_app hardening describes (capture the pid immediately after DispatchEx, guard the property sets, _kill_app on failure). CLAUDE.md already notes the session orphan reaper cannot see such a process because it is a child of DCOM rather than of us. User-visible cost: a ~175 MB headless Excel that never exits. STILL NOT PINNED to a trigger: 20872 appeared at 17:20:55, inside m014's window - a row whose convert_excel toggle was never applied - so the spawning path is worth identifying before fixing. Reproduce by running the office lane alone and watching for an EXCEL.EXE that survives a COMPLETED row.
